statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail 24% remains at the top of the 20-24 watch band and below the 25% block threshold.
recommendation: Tail holds at 24% despite a third successive lower low at 30,580.00, because the new evidence since the previous hour cuts both ways: price retraced roughly 25 to 40 points off the low rather than pinning to it, the DAX opened up 0.06%, and E-mini S&P futures are down only 0.43% against the Nasdaq-100's 0.92%. The selling is concentrated in the AI and semiconductor complex rather than expressed index-wide. The identified checkpoint is the 13:00Z-16:00Z window covering the 13:30Z cash open and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release, where U.S. chipmakers price the OpenAI training pause for the first time. Stress holds at 80% on Brent above $106, a 30-year yield near 2004 highs and an unresolved AI-capex question ahead of core PCE, ISM and payrolls.
headline: NQ extends to a fresh 30,580.00 session low, -0.92% from settle, but retraces off it while the DAX opens +0.06% and ES holds -0.43%; Tail stays at 24% as the OpenAI training pause keeps weakness concentrated in chipmakers
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 30,605.50 on the 07:17Z Yahoo Finance quote and 30,621.00 on the Investing.com quote, 268.25 to 283.75 points and 0.87% to 0.92% below Friday's 30,889.25 settlement. Both feeds now show a session low of 30,580.00 to 30,581.00, roughly 31 points beneath the 30,611.75 low that was current at the previous assessment and 58 points beneath the 30,638.50 low set around 03:00Z. That is a third successive lower low with no reclaimed retracement, and the dominant mode stays trend-down.

Tail nevertheless holds at 24 rather than crossing into the 25-34 block band, because the evidence that arrived since the previous hour cuts both ways. Price has already retraced roughly 25 to 40 points off the new low rather than pinning to it, which is the signature of a functioning retracement rather than a failed one. The full Globex range of 339.75 points is 1.10% of settle across more than nine hours, a drift rather than the persistent no-retracement path this score is designed to flag.

The more important new evidence is the European cash open, which had not occurred at the previous assessment. The DAX trades at 25,410.30, up 0.06% on the session, and E-mini S&P futures at 7,770.25 are down only 0.43%, under half the Nasdaq-100 decline. Cross-asset confirmation is therefore weaker now than an hour ago, not stronger: the selling is concentrated in the AI and semiconductor complex rather than expressed as an index-wide one-way repricing. Asia closed mixed on the same theme, with the Kospi down 2.3%, the CSI 300 down 2% and the Shanghai Composite down 1.5% against a Hang Seng up 0.7% and a Nikkei down 0.1%; Taiwan was closed for Confucius Birthday, so TSMC did not trade.

The driver is the OpenAI decision to pause training, evaluation and inference with tool use for its most capable models while it strengthens safety controls. SK Hynix fell 4.8% and Samsung Electronics 4.6% on that news. U.S. semiconductor names have not yet traded it, which is why the identified checkpoint remains the 13:00Z to 16:00Z window covering the 13:30Z cash open and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release.

Stress holds at 80. Brent trades at 106.95 dollars, up 2.52%, after President Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and Saudi Arabia intercepted drones and missiles aimed at energy infrastructure. The 30-year Treasury yield is near 5.52%, close to its highest since 2004, with the 10-year at 5.18% and the 2-year at 4.87% on the latest H.15 observation. The week carries JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence on Tuesday, core PCE on Wednesday, ISM Manufacturing on Thursday and payrolls on Friday. Against that, the VIX last closed at 14.87, a notably calm reading that argues the options market is not yet pricing a disorderly path.

Shared Finviz context was read and is partial: futures and calendar sections were unavailable, and the file's collection time of 05:58:30Z is more than 92 minutes old, past the 90-minute freshness threshold, so it was treated as stale supporting context only. Its latest-session breadth showed Technology up 0.85% and Semiconductors up 0.56% with Qualcomm up 3.97% and Intel down 3.45%, which is Friday's tape and not evidence of current NQ structure.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail held at 6-8% through the Sunday European and U.S. hours, drifted to 9-14% across the Globex reopen while Stress climbed from 57% to 76%, eased to 9-12% between 00:00Z and 02:00Z, then stepped to 21% at 03:00Z when NQ first took out Friday's low, 22% at 04:00Z, back to 21% at 05:00Z and up to 24% at 06:00Z as the overnight low broke. Dominant mode was normal for twenty of the twenty-four hours, mixed at 02:00Z and 05:00Z and trend-down at 03:00Z, 04:00Z and 06:00Z. Twenty hours mapped to EA_ON and the most recent four to WATCH.
outlookSummary: The published horizon runs from the 07:00Z hour on 28 September through 06:00Z on 29 September. Tail holds in the 20-24 watch band for twenty of the twenty-four hours, reaches the 25-34 elevated band for the three hours from 13:00Z to 15:00Z, and drops to 19% in the low band only for the 21:00Z CME maintenance break, when no meaningful price discovery exists. The peak of 27% falls on the 14:00Z hour covering post-open continuation risk and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release. Those three elevated hours carry the event/whipsaw mode, and their named conditional risk is opening-auction extension with a failed first retracement as U.S. semiconductor names price the OpenAI training pause. Stress holds between 76% and 82% throughout, reflecting the Hormuz oil premium, a 30-year yield near 2004 highs and an unresolved AI-capex question ahead of a week carrying JOLTS, core PCE, ISM Manufacturing and payrolls. Confidence peaks at 83% during European and U.S. cash hours and troughs at 74-76% across the maintenance break and the far edge of the horizon.
